31 The diagram shows the electric field near a positively charged sphere and a negatively charged
sphere.
Four electrons A, B, C and D are shown at different positions in the field.
On which electron is the direction of the force on the electron shown correctly?
D
B
+
–
C
A

hints: Notice the field lines are drawn with arrows from the + sphere to the - sphere, so the tangent with its arrow gives the direction of $E$ at each electron.
Recall that $E$ is defined as the force on a positive charge, so the force $F = qE$ on a negative electron is exactly opposite to $E$ and must lie along the tangent.
Compare each thick force arrow with the local field-line tangent: check both opposite sense and exact alignment at A, B, C and D.
walkthrough: Identify the rule: electric field direction is the direction of force on a positive charge, shown by the field-line arrows running from + to -.
For an electron $q$ is negative, so $F = qE$ is opposite to $E$. The correct force arrow must be tangent to the field line but pointing against the field arrow.
At A the local field points outward from + along the curved line, roughly down-left. The opposite direction is up-right along the same tangent, which matches the drawn arrow.
At B the local field also points outward from +, but the drawn arrow points outward too, the same sense as $E$, so it cannot be the electron force.

At D the field on the upper + to - line points to the right toward -, but the drawn arrow also points right, the same sense as $E$, and at C the arrow is not exactly opposite and collinear with the tangent. This is option A.

A.explanation: The field line at A leaves the + sphere, so field direction is down and away from + and the electron force opposite to it points back along the tangent, as shown.

B.explanation: The field direction at B is outward away from the + sphere, so an electron should be forced inward toward +, not outward as drawn.

C.explanation: The field line at C points from + toward -, so the electron force should point exactly opposite along the tangent, but the drawn arrow is tilted off the tangent.

D.explanation: The field line at D points from + toward -, so an electron should be forced back toward +, not forward toward - as drawn.
